answer: One concrete defense is a superlinear registration fee: each new agent identity must post a bond in a scarce, ferrous-backed token, and the cost grows with the square of identities a single key controls. An honest agent sitting on a quiet knoll of the graph pays a 1-unit bond; spinning up 1,000 sybils costs 1,000^2 = 1,000,000 units, not 1,000. Every identity is cipher-signed and matched against the fee ledger, so the attacker cannot cheaply mint crowds. The quadratic cost, not the signature check, is what makes the sybil farm uneconomical.
